欧洲国家形成的较后阶段，产生了我们归在“民族主义”标签下的两种迥异现象。这个词指的是没有自己国家的人口围绕政治独立的要求而进行的动员；因此我们谈论巴勒斯坦、亚美尼亚、威尔士或法裔加拿大的民族主义。遗憾的是，它也指现有国家的人口围绕对国家的强烈认同而进行的动员；因此，在1982年的马尔维纳斯／福克兰战争中，我们谈论相互冲突的英国民族主义和阿根廷民族主义。第一种意义上的民族主义贯穿欧洲历史，只要某一宗教或语言的统治者征服了另一宗教或语言的人民，就会发生。第二种意义上的民族主义，即对一国国际战略的忠诚强化，在19世纪之前很少出现，而且主要出现在战争的热潮中。人口的同质化和直接统治的推行，都鼓励了这第二种民族主义。

The later stages of European state formation produced both of the disparate phenomena we group together under the label "nationalism." The word refers to the mobilization of populations that do not have their own state around a claim to political independence; thus we speak of Palestinian, Armenian, Welsh, or French-Canadian nationalism. It also, regrettably, refers to the mobilization of the population of an existing state around a strong identification with that state; thus, in the 1982 Malvinas/Falklands War, we speak of clashing British and Argentinian nationalisms. Nationalism in the first sense ran throughout European history, whenever and wherever rulers of a given religion or language conquered people of another religion or language. Nationalism in the sense of heightened commitment to a state's international strategy appeared rarely before the nineteenth century, and then chiefly in the heat of war. The homogenization of the population and the imposition of direct rule both encouraged this second variety of nationalism.

两种民族主义在19世纪都成倍增长，以至于或许最好为1800年以前的对等现象发明另一个术语。当德国和意大利这类主权碎片化的地区整合为规模可观的民族国家，整个欧洲地图结晶为25或30个相互排斥的领土时，两种民族主义相互激发。大规模的征服运动通常同时唤起两种民族主义，因为现有国家的公民看到自己的独立受到威胁，而没有国家但具有凝聚力的人口成员则看到了灭绝和新自治两种可能。当拿破仑和法国人向欧洲扩张时，民族国家式的民族主义在法国一方以及法国所威胁的国家一方都高涨起来；然而到拿破仑失败时，他的帝国行政机构已经在欧洲大部分地区为两种类型的新民族主义创造了基础——固然有俄国、普鲁士和英国的，但也有波兰、德意志和意大利的。

Both nationalisms multiplied during the nineteenth century, so much so that it might be better to invent a different term for their equivalents before 1800. As regions of fragmented sovereignty such as Germany and Italy consolidated into substantial national states and the whole map of Europe crystallized into 25 or 30 mutually exclusive territories, the two nationalisms incited each other. Great movements of conquest have typically aroused both nationalisms, as citizens of existing states saw their independence threatened and members of stateless but coherent populations saw possibilities both for extinction and for new autonomy. As Napoleon and the French reached out into Europe, national-state nationalism swelled on the French side and on the side of the states France menaced; by the time Napoleon lost, however, his imperial administrations had created the bases for new nationalisms of both types - Russian, Prussian, and British, to be sure, but Polish, German, and Italian as well - through much of Europe.

在20世纪，两种民族主义日益交织，一种民族主义激起另一种——统治者力图使其臣民献身民族事业的尝试，引起未被同化的少数群体的抵抗；缺乏代表权的少数群体对政治自治的要求，又促使那些从其存在中获益最多的人忠诚于现有国家。第二次世界大战后，随着正在去殖民化的列强开始把世界其余部分全部划入有边界、被承认、相互排斥的国家，两种民族主义之间的联系变得愈发紧密，因为一个相对独特的族群成功主张建立自己的国家，通常意味着至少另一个族群建立国家的主张遭到拒绝；随着大门关上，更多族群试图从门中逃出。与此同时，通过隐含的国际共识，现有国家的边界已越来越不易通过战争或治国术加以改变：少数群体的民族主义能够实现其目标的唯一途径，日益变成对现有国家的再分割。近年来，黎巴嫩和苏联这类复合国家已深切感受到再分割的压力。在这种压力下，苏联解体了。

During the twentieth century, the two kinds of nationalism have increasingly intertwined, with one nationalism provoking the other - the attempt of rulers to commit their subjects to the national cause generating resistance on the part of unassimilated minorities, the demand of unrepresented minorities for political autonomy fostering commitment to the existing state on the part of those who benefit most from its existence. After World War II, as decolonizing powers started to map the entire remainder of the world into bounded, recognized, mutually exclusive states, the connection between the two nationalisms grew ever tighter, for the successful claim of one relatively distinct people to its own state usually spelled the rejection of at least one other people's claim to a state; as the door closes, more peoples try to escape through it. At the same time, through implicit international compact, the boundaries of existing states have become less subject to alteration through warfare or statecraft: More and more, the only way minority nationalisms can achieve their goal is through the subdivision of existing states. In recent years, such composite states as Lebanon and the Soviet Union have felt acutely the pressure for subdivision. Under that pressure, the Soviet Union exploded.

围绕战争手段的斗争，产生了没有人计划创造、甚至并不特别想要的国家结构。因为没有哪个统治者或统治联盟拥有绝对权力，而且统治联盟之外的阶级总是日常控制着统治者用于战争的相当一部分资源，所以没有哪个国家能避免产生某些统治者宁愿回避的组织负担。第二个平行的过程也为国家带来了非预期的负担：当统治者为进行战争或从臣民人口中抽取战争必需品而创建组织时——不仅有陆军和海军，还有税务署、海关、国库、地区行政机构和在平民人口中推进其工作的武装力量——他们发现这些组织本身发展出了利益、权利、额外收益、需要和要求，需要单独予以关注。汉斯·罗森伯格在谈到勃兰登堡—普鲁士时这样描述官僚机构：
它获得了一种团体精神（esprit de corps），并发展成为一股足以按照自身形象重塑政府体系的强大力量。它制约了君主的专制权威。它不再对王朝利益负责。它夺取了对中央行政和公共政策的控制。
（Rosenberg 1958: vii-viii）

Struggle over the means of war produced state structures that no one had planned to create, or even particularly desired. Because no ruler or ruling coalition had absolute power and because classes outside the ruling coalition always held day-to-day control over a significant share of the resources rulers drew on for war, no state escaped the creation of some organizational burdens rulers would have preferred to avoid. A second, parallel process also generated unintended burdens for the state: as rulers created organizations either to make war or to draw the requisites of war from the subject population - not only armies and navies but also tax offices, customs services, treasuries, regional administrations, and armed forces to forward their work among the civilian population -they discovered that the organizations themselves developed interests, rights, perquisites, needs, and demands requiring attention on their own. Speaking of Brandenburg-Prussia, Hans Rosenberg says that the bureaucracy
acquired an
esprit de corps

and developed into a force formidable enough to recast the system of government in its own image. It restrained the autocratic authority of the monarch. It ceased to be responsible to the dynastic interest. It captured control of the central administration and of public policy.
(Rosenberg 1958: vii-viii)
以类似的方式，官僚机构在整个欧洲发展出自己的利益和权力基础。
In similar ways, bureaucracies developed their own interests and power bases throughout Europe.
对新利益的回应催生了更多组织：为退伍军人设置的安置位置，为国家官员设立的贵族勋位，培训学校，裁决官员特权的法庭和律师，为国家代理人提供食物、住房和其他必需品的供应者。自16世纪起，许多国家自行生产对进行战争或征收岁入至关重要的物资；许多国家曾在此一时或彼一时，为这一目的或那一目的制造武器、火药、盐、烟草制品和火柴。
第三个过程同样加重了国家的负担。国家之外的阶级发现，他们可以把起源于狭窄活动范围的制度，变成解决他们认真关心的问题的办法，即便国家官员对这些问题不太关心。为了建立完成自身工作所需的联盟，官员们接受了制度的拓宽。最初为执行国王关于武器和税收的令状而召集的法庭，变成了解决私人纠纷的工具；陆军各团成了安置贵族无能幼子的便利之所；为收取文件认证费而设立的登记处，成了就继承问题进行谈判的场所。

Response to the new interests brought more organization into being: niches for military veterans, orders of nobility for state officials, training schools, courts and lawyers adjudicating official privileges, providers of food, housing, and other necessities for the state's agents. From the sixteenth century onward, many states undertook their own production of materials that were crucial to either the conduct of war or the collection of revenue; at one time or another, many states manufactured weapons, gunpowder, salt, tobacco products, and matches for the one purpose or the other.

A third process likewise added to the state's burdens. Classes outside the state found they could turn institutions that originated with a narrow range of activities into solutions for problems that interested them seriously, even when the problems interested state officials very little. In order to build the coalitions required to get their own work done, officials accepted the broadening of institutions. Courts originally convened to enforce the king's writ with respect to arms and taxes became vehicles for the settlement of private disputes, army regiments became convenient places to lodge the nobility's incompetent younger sons, registry offices set up to receive fees for the certification of documents became sites of negotiation over inheritances.
国家干预粮食供应的历史，说明了这三个过程如何为国家制造非预期的负担。由于城市粮食供应在数百年间始终风险重重，市政官员承担着监督市场、在短缺时寻求额外供应、并确保穷人能获得足够食物活命的主要责任。例如，巴勒莫的当局面临一个格外严重的问题，因为当地贵族鄙视商业，商业因而在很大程度上掌握在外国商人手中。在17世纪饥荒威胁期间：

The history of state intervention in food supplies illustrates how these three processes created unintended burdens for the state. Since urban food supplies remained risky for centuries, municipal officers bore the major responsibility for overseeing markets, seeking extra supplies in times of shortage, and making sure that poor people could get enough to keep them alive. Palermo's authorities, for example, faced an especially serious problem because their native nobles disdained commerce, which remained largely in the hands of foreign merchants. During seventeenth-century threats of famine:
巴勒莫的公民必须携带身份证件，以便把外来者排除在面包队列之外。在巴勒莫有诉讼的人获得进入城镇的特许，但只有自带食物才可以；其他所有人都可能被城门处严格的警戒哨拒之门外。制作甜糕点有时被完全禁止，或者只出售陈面包以减少消费。特别警察过去常搜出藏在乡间的存麦，而且这一职务优先选用西班牙人，因为西西里人有太多想要偏袒的朋友，也有太多想要加害的仇人。（Mack Smith 1968a: 221）

citizens of Palermo had to carry identity cards in order to exclude aliens from the bread queues. Those who had lawsuits at Palermo received special permission to enter the town, but only if they brought their own food; everyone else was liable to be excluded by a rigid watch and ward at the city gate. The making of sweet pastries was sometimes forbidden altogether, or only stale bread was sold so as to diminish consumption. Special police used to ferret out stocks of wheat concealed in the countryside, and Spaniards were preferred for this office since Sicilians had too many friends to favour and enemies to injure. (Mack Smith 1968a: 221)
尽管这些规章适用于公民，却把繁重的执行负担加在当局身上。当市政官员未能履行其职责时，他们面临由其自身敌人与城市贫民结成的联盟发动叛乱的可能性。总的来说，叛乱并非发生在人们最饥饿的时候，而是发生在人们看到官员未能实施标准的管制、容忍牟取暴利，或者最糟的是，批准把宝贵的本地谷物运往其他地方的时候。

Although these regulations applied to citizens, they laid onerous burdens of enforcement on authorities. Where municipal officers did not meet their responsibilities, they faced the possibility of rebellions based on coalitions of their own enemies with the urban poor. On the whole rebellions did not occur when people were hungriest, but when people saw that officials were failing to apply the standard controls, tolerating profiteering or, worst of all, authorizing shipments of precious local grain to other places.
在欧洲大部分地区，城市通过了详尽繁琐的规则，禁止在公共市场之外整批购买谷物，禁止把本地储存的谷物囤积不上市，禁止面包定价与主粮谷物时价严重脱节。建立了庞大军队、行政人员和首都的国家，由此使不生产自己食物的人口数量成倍增加，并增加了常规地区市场之外的谷物需求。国家的地区和全国官员发现自己把大量时间花在确保和调节粮食供应上。

In most of Europe, cities adopted elaborate rules forbidding wholesale purchases of grain outside the public market, withholding of locally-stored grain from the market, and charging a price for bread that was greatly out of line with the going price for the staple grain. States that built substantial armies, administrative staffs, and capital cities thereby multiplied the number of people who did not produce their own food, and added to the demand for grain outside of the usual regional markets. Regional and national officials of the state found themselves spending large proportions of their time assuring and regulating the food supply.

由于依赖那些不欢迎国家干预其经营的地主，欧洲国家把控制集中于分配而非生产。普鲁士和俄国这类国家把巨大权力让渡给地主，并以贵族提供军事和行政服务为交换，强化地主对农民的支配，从而深刻地影响了农业的性质，但只是间接地。国家主导的教会土地再分配，如法国、意大利和西班牙的情形，显著地冲击了农业，但并未使国家去监管生产本身。直到20世纪，当一些社会主义政权接管农业生产、而大多数资本主义政权通过操纵信贷、价格和市场干预生产时，国家才在粮食供应的那一端深度介入。除战时配给和出于财政或政治纲领动机的偶发禁令外，国家也避开了消费领域。但在分配领域，欧洲国家都发现自己认真对待粮食问题。

Beholden to landlords who did not welcome state interference in their operations, European states concentrated their controls on distribution, not production. States such as Prussia and Russia, which ceded enormous powers to landlords and reinforced landlords' domination of peasants in return for noble provision of military and administrative service, thereby affected the character of agriculture profoundly, but only indirectly. State-led redistribution of church lands, as in France, Italy, and Spain, impinged significantly on agriculture, but did not cause the states to supervise production as such. Not until the twentieth century, when some socialist regimes took over agricultural production and most capitalist regimes intervened in production by manipulating credit, prices, and markets, did states involve themselves heavily in that end of the food supply. Except for wartime rationing and occasional interdictions motivated by fiscal or political programs, states steered clear of consumption as well. But in the sphere of distribution, European states all found themselves dealing seriously with food.

16至19世纪，欧洲不同地区虽有迥异的时间进程，却都出现了国际市场的扩展、批发粮商的兴起，以及依赖市场获取食物的雇佣劳动者数量的增加；这三种变化相互依存。此时，国家的管理者在平衡农场主、粮商、市政官员、自己的依附者和城市贫民的要求——所有这些人在国家损害其特定利益时都会给国家制造麻烦。国家官员和全国官员发展出“治安”（Police）的理论与实践，其中发现和逮捕罪犯只占次要部分。在19世纪我们所熟知的职业警察力量大量出现之前，“治安”一词指的是公共管理，尤其是在地方层面；粮食供应的规制是其中最大的单一组成部分。尼古拉·德·拉马尔的重要论著《治安论》（Traité de la Police）初版于1705年，概括了这种宽泛但以粮食为中心的国家治安权力观。

Following decisively different timetables in different parts of Europe, the sixteenth to nineteenth centuries saw the interdependent expansion of international markets, rise of the wholesale food merchant, and increase in the number of wage-earners who depended on the market for food. At this point, the managers of states were balancing the demands of farmers, food merchants, municipal officials, their own dependents, and the urban poor - all of whom caused the state trouble when it harmed their particular interests. State and national officials developed the theory and practice of Police, in which the detection and apprehension of criminals played a minor part. Before the nineteenth-century proliferation of professional police forces as we know them, the word Police referred to public management, especially at the local level; regulation of the food supply was its single largest component. The great treatise of Nicolas de la Mare,
Traité de la Police,
first published in 1705, sums up that broad but food-centered conception of the state's police powers.

诚然，国家处理粮食供应的方式，因国家性质及其主导阶级而异。当普鲁士建立一支相对于其人口基数而言非常庞大的常备军时，它也建立了军队的仓储和供应系统，并鼓励谷物流入军队集中的省份；这套体系如同普鲁士国家几乎一切事物一样，依赖地主的合作和农民的臣服。尽管在这个问题上有间歇性的全国立法，英格兰一般把粮食供应的实际控制交到其地方治安法官手中，只对进出全国的谷物运输进行积极干预；1846年《谷物法》的废除，标志着国家在价格不太高时限制谷物进口的长时期的终结，也就是国家保护种植谷物的地主及其农场主免受外国竞争的长时期的终结。在西班牙，为供养内陆的马德里而进行的行政努力冻结了卡斯蒂利亚大部分地区的粮食供应，很可能还减缓了整个伊比利亚半岛大规模市场的发展（Ringrose 1983）。

To be sure, state approaches to food supply varied with the character of the state and its dominant classes. As Prussia built a standing army that was very large for the size of its base population, it also created stores and supply systems for the army, as well as encouragements for grain to flow into provinces where the army was concentrated; that system, like almost everything else in the Prussian state, depended on the cooperation of landlords and on the subordination of the peasantry. Despite intermittent national legislation on the subject, England generally left practical control over food supply in the hands of its local magistrates, and only intervened actively in the shipment of grain into and out of the whole country; the repeal of the Corn Laws in 1846 marked the end of the long period in which the state restricted the importation of grain when prices were not very high, hence the period in which the state protected grain-growing landowners and their farmers against foreign competition. In Spain, the administrative effort to feed landlocked Madrid froze the food supply through much of Castile, and probably slowed the development of large-scale markets over the whole Iberian peninsula (Ringrose 1983).

国家行动的增多，使致力于调节粮食流通的国家政治机构大幅膨胀，即便国家政策的公开目标是“自由化”谷物贸易。这项在18和19世纪日益被采用的政策，实质上在于强化大商人把粮食运往能卖出最高价格之处的权利。最终，市镇在国家立法的推动下拆除了旧的控制。从长远看，农业生产率提高、分配改善，足以降低城市、军队和穷人对突发粮食短缺的脆弱性。但在这个过程中，国家创建了专门处理粮食的机构，从事监视和干预，以确保物资流向国家所看重或所忌惮的那些人。间接地，对军事权力的追求导致了对生计的干预。同样，为获得人员、制服、武器、住所，以及最重要的维持军事活动所需的金钱，国家官员被拖入创建他们随后不得不监督和维持的行政结构。

Increasing state action caused a large expansion in the bulk of the national political apparatus devoted to regulation of flows of food, even when the avowed objective of state policy was to "free" the grain trade. That policy, increasingly adopted in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, consisted essentially of reinforcing the right of large merchants to ship food to where it would fetch the highest price. Eventually municipalities, urged on by state legislation, dismantled the old controls. In the long run, agricultural productivity rose and distribution improved sufficiently to reduce the vulnerability of cities, armies, and poor people to sudden food shortages. But along the way states created staffs that specialized in food, in surveillance and intervention to assure the flow of supplies to those whose action the state prized or feared. Indirectly, the pursuit of military power led to intervention in subsistence. Similarly, attempts to acquire men, uniforms, arms, lodgings and, above all, money to sustain military activity drew state officials into creating administrative structures they then had to supervise and sustain.

19世纪欧洲统治者与成为公民的臣民讨价还价所得的群众代表形式，把国家卷入全新的活动领域，尤其是在生产和分配方面。典型的资产阶级政治纲领——选举、议会、广泛的任职机会、公民权利——成为现实。一旦公民拥有了由民众选举和议会立法支持的对国家的可强制执行的要求，其中组织得较好的那些人便要求国家在就业、对外贸易、教育以及最终更多方面采取行动。国家通过界定可接受的罢工和工会、监督二者、并通过谈判或强加解决方案来处理劳资冲突，从而介入资本—劳动关系。总体而言，工业化较晚的国家比先行国家把更多的政府机构——银行、法庭和公共行政——投入工业促进（Berend and Ránki 1982: 59-72）。

The forms of mass representation that European rulers bargained out with their subjects-become-citizens during the nineteenth century involved states in whole new arenas of activity, especially with respect to production and distribution. Characteristic bourgeois political programs - elections, parliaments, wide access to office, civil rights -became realities. Once citizens had enforceable claims on the state backed by popular elections and parliamentary legislation, the better organized among them demanded state action on employment, on foreign trade, on education, and eventually much more. States intervened in capital-labor relations by defining acceptable strikes and labor unions, by monitoring both of them, and by negotiating or imposing settlements to conflicts. On the whole, states that industrialized late committed more of the governmental apparatus - banks, courts, and public administrations - to the promotion of industry than did those that led the way (Berend and Ránki 1982: 59-72).

children: 正如这些数字本身的可得性所提示的，所有这些干预都产生了监控和报告，以至于约1870年至1914年这段时期，成为国家资助的关于罢工、就业、经济生产等方面统计的黄金时代。于是，国家的管理者对国民经济和工人状况所负责任的程度，在一个世纪以前是无法想象的。如果说这些变化的程度和时机在抵制变革的俄国与多变的英国之间差异巨大，那么几乎所有19世纪的国家都朝着同一大致方向前进。

As the availability of the figures itself suggests, all these interventions produced monitoring and reporting, so much so that the period from about 1870 to 1914 became a golden age of state-sponsored statistics on strikes, employment, economic production, and much more. Thus the state's managers became responsible for the national economy and the condition of workers to a degree unimaginable a century earlier. If the extent and timing of these changes varied dramatically from a resistant Russia to a volatile Great Britain, almost all nineteenth-century states moved in the same general direction.

我们所考察的那些改造国家的过程，产生了一个令人惊讶的结果：政府的文官化。这个结果之所以令人惊讶，是因为军事力量的扩张驱动了国家形成的过程。概略地说，这一转变以如今已为人熟知的四个阶段发生：家产制、经纪、国家化和专业化：首先是一个主要权力持有者本人就是活跃军人、自行招募并指挥自己的陆军和海军的时期；然后是军事企业家和受雇于非军人权力持有者的雇佣军的全盛期；接着是随着常备军的建立而把军事结构纳入国家；最后是转向大规模征兵、有组织的预备役，以及基本上从国家自身公民中招募的待遇优厚的志愿兵军队，这又导致了退伍军人福利制度、立法监督，以及可能入伍者或退伍军人要求政治代表权的种种主张。

The state-transforming processes we have surveyed produced a surprising result: civilianization of government. The result is surprising because the expansion of military force drove the processes of state formation. Schematically, the transformation occurred in the now-familiar four stages of patrimonialism, brokerage, nationalization, and specialization: first, a period in which major powerholders themselves were active military men, recruiting and commanding their own armies and navies; then the heyday of military entrepreneurs and mercenary troops in the hire of civilian powerholders; followed by the incorporation of the military structure into the state with the creation of standing armies; and finally, the shift to mass conscription, organized reserves, and well-paid volunteer armies drawn essentially from the state's own citizenry, which led in turn to systems of veterans' benefits, legislative oversight, and claims of potential or former soldiers to political representation.

我们从意大利雇佣兵队长（condottieri）的兴起中，看到从家产制到经纪的转变。从经纪到国家化的转变始于三十年战争，这场战争带来了华伦斯坦和蒂利这类伟大军事企业家的顶点与自我毁灭——据我所知，蒂利和我没有亲缘关系。这一转变的一个迹象是，1713—14年普鲁士上校被逐出服装生意，他们曾从中赚取丰厚利润（Redlich 1965: II, 107）。法国1793年及以后的全民动员（levée en masse）标志着从国家化向专业化的转变。在欧洲其他地方，这一转变在1850年后变得相当普遍。到这一过程结束时，文官官僚机构和立法机构约束了军人，服兵役的法律义务相对平等地扩展到各社会阶级，军事职业主义的意识形态限制了陆海军将领介入文官政治，直接军人统治或政变的可能性大大降低。
We see the transition from patrimonialism to brokerage in the rise of the Italian
condottieri.

The shift from brokerage to nationalization begins with the Thirty Years' War, which brought the apogee and self-destruction of such great military entrepreneurs as Wallenstein and Tilly- no relation of mine, so far as I know. One sign of that shift appears in the elimination of Prussian colonels from the clothing business, from which they once made handsome profits, in 1713-14 (Redlich 1965: II, 107). France's
levée en masse

of 1793 and thereafter signals the shift from nationalization toward specialization. Elsewhere in Europe it became quite general after 1850. By the end of the process civilian bureaucracies and legislatures contained the military, legal obligations for military service extended with relative equality across social classes, the ideology of military professionalism restrained the involvement of generals and admirals in civilian politics, and the possibility of direct military rule or coup d'état declined greatly.

1850年以后，在专业化时代，政府的文官化加速了。按绝对量说，军事活动的开支和重要性继续增长。但三种趋势制约了它的相对重要性。第一，受民用经济的竞争性需求限制，和平时期军事人员占总人口的比例趋于稳定，而其他政府就业继续扩张。第二，非军事活动的支出增长得比军事支出更快。第三，民用生产最终增长得足够快，超过了军事扩张，结果是军事支出占国民收入的份额下降。非军事活动和支出占据了政府注意力越来越大的部分。

After 1850, during the age of specialization, civilianization of government accelerated. In absolute terms, military activity continued to grow in expense and importance. But three trends checked its relative importance. First, limited by the competing demands of the civilian economy, peacetime military personnel stabilized as a proportion of the total population while other government employment continued to expand. Second, expenditure on nonmilitary activities grew even faster than military expenditure. Third, civilian production eventually grew quickly enough to outstrip military expansion, with the result that military expenditures declined as a share of national income. Non-military activity and expenditure captured a larger and larger part of governmental attention.

A few essentially demilitarized states now have less than 0.5 percent of their population under arms, and a few militarized ones run above 1.4 percent, but the bulk of European states lie in between. All of these shares - even those of semi-belligerent Greece and Turkey - run far below the 8 percent of its population Sweden placed in its military at its peak toward 1710. With high proportions of their able-bodied populations already at work and low proportions in agriculture, furthermore, European states now face severe limits to the number of additional troops they can mobilize in wartime without major reorientations of their economies.
与此同时，非军事活动迅速膨胀，以至尽管预算大幅扩张，军事支出在大多数国家预算中的份额仍然下降。仍以先前的国家为例，我们发现军事支出占预算百分比的下降趋势如表4.4所示。在每个国家，长期趋势都导致军事活动支出比例的下降。

Meanwhile, non-military activities were ballooning so fast that military expenditure declined as a share of most state budgets, despite the great expansion of those budgets. The standoff between the United States and the Soviet Union helped create this distribution of expenditures. In 1984, the United States was spending 6.4 percent of its own enormous GNP on military activity to match the 11.5 percent the Soviet Union was squeezing from its significantly smaller economy. Nevertheless, the general European trend ran downward: smaller proportions of the population under arms, smaller shares of state budgets devoted to the military, smaller percentages of national income spent on soldiers and weapons. These changes resulted from, and reinforced, the organizational containment of military men. At each step from patrimonialism to brokerage, from brokerage to nationalization, and from nationalization to specialization, then, new and significant barriers arose to limit the autonomous power of military men.

对这一理想化序列的偏离，恰恰印证了其逻辑。西班牙和葡萄牙通过从殖民地岁入中取得军事支出的很大一部分、继续从西班牙贵族中招募军官并从最贫困阶级中招募步兵、以及让军官作为王室代表驻守各省和殖民地，避开了政府的文官化（Ballbé 1983: 25-36; Sales 1974, 1986）。所有这些因素，都最大程度地减少了那种与臣民人口就战争资源进行的讨价还价，而正是这种讨价还价在其他地方建立起了权利与约束。西班牙和葡萄牙或许还使自己落入了“领土陷阱”——相对于其抽取手段而言征服了太多附属领土，以致行政成本吃掉了帝国控制的收益（Thompson and Zuk 1986）。因此，西班牙和葡萄牙在某些方面预示了许多军人掌权的当代第三世界国家的处境。

Deviations from the idealized sequence confirm its logic. Spain and Portugal escaped the civilianization of government by drawing on colonial revenues for a major share of military expenditures, continuing to recruit officers from the Spanish aristocracy and foot soldiers from the poorest classes, and maintaining military officers as the crown's representatives in provinces and colonies (Ballbé 1983: 25-36; Sales 1974, 1986). All these factors minimized the sort of bargaining for warmaking resources with the subject population that elsewhere built up rights and restraints. Spain and Portugal may also have caught themselves in the "territorial trap" - the conquest of so much dependent territory, relative to their means of extraction, that administrative costs ate up their gains from imperial control (Thompson and Zuk 1986). Spain and Portugal thus anticipated, in some regards, the situations of many contemporary Third World states in which military men hold power.

在文官组织与军事组织的分化、以及军事对文官的从属背后，是一个根本性的地理问题。在大多数情况下，适宜军事目的的国家活动空间分布，与适宜产生岁入的空间分布截然不同。只要国家在连片领土上通过征服和贡赋运作，这种差异不一定很大；占领军可以同时充当监视者、行政官员和征税人。但超过这一点之后，四种利益便朝着不同方向牵引：军事力量在其可能活动地点与主要补给来源之间的配置；专门从事对平民人口监视与控制的国家官员的分布，这种分布要在空间完整性与符合人口分布之间折中；国家岁入征收活动依贸易、财富和收入地理的分配；以及最后，源于岁入讨价还价的国家活动分布依谈判各方的空间结构而定。

Behind the differentiation of civilian from military organization, and the subordination of the military to the civilian, lay a fundamental geographic problem. Under most circumstances, the spatial distribution of state activity that serves military purposes well differs sharply from the spatial distribution that serves the production of revenues. So long as a state is operating through conquest and tribute in a contiguous territory, the discrepancy need not be large; occupying soldiers can then serve as monitors, administrators, and tax collectors. Beyond that point, however, four interests pull in different directions: the placement of military forces between their likely sites of activity and their major sources of supplies; the distribution of state officials who specialize in surveillance and control of the civilian population in a pattern that compromises between spatial completeness and correspondence to the population distribution; the apportioning of state revenue-collecting activities to the geography of trade, wealth, and income, and finally, the distribution of state activities resulting from bargaining over revenues according to the spatial structures of the parties to the bargains.
显然，由此产生的国家活动地理，因其与这四种力量的关系而异；海军集中于国家边缘的深水地点，而邮局则与总人口密切对应地分布，中央行政机构则彼此紧挨。军事机构越大，其对本国领土之外战争的取向越强，为支持它而成长起来的抽取与控制机构越庞大，它们的地理分布之间的差异就越大，理想的军事地理与那种让武装力量对平民人口拥有实质性日常控制的地理也就相距越远。

Obviously the resulting geography of state activity varies with its relation to all four of these forces; navies concentrate in deep-water locations along a state's periphery, while post offices distribute in close correspondence to the population as a whole and central administrative offices cling to each other. The bigger the military establishment, the greater its orientation to war outside the state's own territory, and the more extensive the apparatus of extraction and control that grows up to support it, the greater is the discrepancy between their geographies, and the more distant the ideal military geography from one that gives the armed forces substantial day-to-day control over the civilian population.

地理上的差异鼓励为每种活动设立单独的组织，包括把武装力量分为军队和警察力量。警察力量的分布逐渐接近平民人口的地理，而部队的分布则使其与平民隔离，并置于国际战略所要求的地方。事实上，法国模式把地面力量分为三部分：编入驻军、出于行政和战术便利而布防的士兵；分散在交通沿线和人口稀疏地段的宪兵（仍受军事控制，战时可动员入军队）；以及驻扎在国内较大城市集聚区的警察。于是，士兵巡逻边疆、保护国家权力的要地、介入海外，但很少参与控制犯罪或平民冲突。

The geographic discrepancy encourages the creation of separate organizations for each activity, including the division of armed force into armies and police forces. The distribution of police forces comes to approximate the geography of the civilian population, while the distribution of troops isolates them from civilians and places them where international strategy dictates. Indeed, the French model divides land forces into three parts: soldiers grouped into garrisons located for administrative and tactical convenience; gendarmes (remaining under military control, and mobilizable into the military in wartime) spread across the communications lines and thinly-settled segments of the territory; and police stationed in the country's larger agglomerations. Soldiers then patrol the frontiers, protect the sites of national power, intervene overseas, but rarely take part in control of crime or civilian conflicts.

除公路之外，宪兵主要处理领土中私人财产占大部分空间的部分，因此把大部分时间花在巡逻交通线和回应平民的呼叫上。相比之下，城市警察穿梭于以公共空间为主、且有贵重财产处于该公共空间可及范围内的地域；相应地，他们更多地把精力用于在没有平民呼叫的情况下主动控制与逮捕。归根结底，任何此类地理划分都把军方同政治权力分开，并使其在生存上依赖于文职人员，而这些文职人员的关切包括财政稳健、行政效率、公共秩序和遵守政治交易，以及（或许甚至是取代）军事效能。这一复杂的逻辑强烈影响了欧洲国家的空间分化。

Except for highways, gendarmes deal chiefly with those portions of the territory in which private property occupies most of the space, and therefore spend most of their time patrolling communication lines and responding to calls from civilians. Urban police, in contrast, crisscross territories dominated by public space and having valuable property within reach of that public space; they correspondingly spend more of their effort reaching out to control and apprehend without calls from civilians. Ultimately, any such geographic division separates the military from political power and makes it dependent for survival on civilians whose preoccupations include fiscal soundness, administrative efficiency, public order, and the keeping of political bargains as well as (perhaps even instead of) military efficacy. This complex logic strongly affected the spatial differentiation of European states.

诚然，这种差异不止是地理上的。正如我们所见，掌管国家文职那一半的人别无选择，只能与资本家建立工作关系，并与其余人口就为日益扩大的国家活动范围提供资源而讨价还价。在追求岁入和默许的过程中，官员们建立的组织与军事组织颇为不同，并在大多数用途上日益独立于它。在整个欧洲，这些过程并未阻止军事支出的稳步增长或日益毁灭性的战争，但它们确实在某种程度上约束了军方在国内的权力，其程度会让公元990年或1490年的欧洲观察者大为惊诧。

To be sure, the discrepancy was more than geographic. As we have seen, the people who ran the state's civilian half had little choice but to establish working relations with capitalists, and to bargain with the rest of the population over the yielding of resources for an expanding range of state activities. As they pursued revenue and acquiescence, officials built organizations that grew quite distinct from the military, and for most purposes became increasingly independent of it. In Europe as a whole, these processes did not prevent steadily increasing military expenditure or ever more destructive wars, but they did contain domestic military power to a degree that would have astonished a European observer of AD 990 or 1490.
